extracted.intended_audience: attorneys, parties, experts, and non-parties in patent litigation (Northern District of California)
extracted.subtask_description: A court-form protective order governing designation, access, use, challenge, and final disposition of confidential, highly confidential, and source-code materials in patent litigation, including procedures for experts, house counsel, subpoenas, and source-code inspection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duration of confidentiality obligations
rubrics_metrics.description: Even after final disposition of this litigation, the confidentiality obligations imposed by this Order shall remain in effect until a Designating Party agrees otherwise in writing or a court order otherwise directs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Final disposition is the later of (1) dismissal of all claims and defenses in this action, with or without prejudice; and (2) final judgment after completion and exhaustion of all appeals, rehearings, remands, trials, or reviews of this action, including time limits for filing motions or applications for extension of time pursuant to applicable law.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exercise of restraint and care in designating material for protection
rubrics_metrics.description: Each Party or Non-Party that designates information or items for protection under this Order must take care to limit any such designation to specific material that qualifies under the appropriate standards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Designate only those parts of material that qualify; mass, indiscriminate, or routinized designations are prohibited and may expose the Designating Party to sanctions. If a designation is mistaken or no longer qualifies, the Designating Party must promptly notify others and withdraw the mistaken designation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manner and timing of designations for documentary materials
rubrics_metrics.description: Disclosure or Discovery Material that qualifies for protection under this Order must be clearly so designated before the material is disclosed or produced, except as otherwise provided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For documentary information (paper or electronic but excluding transcripts), the Producing Party must affix the legend “CONFIDENTIAL,” “HIGHLY CONFIDENTIAL – ATTORNEYS’ EYES ONLY,” or “HIGHLY CONFIDENTIAL – SOURCE CODE” to each page containing protected material. If only portions of a page qualify, the Producing Party must clearly identify the protected portions (e.g., markings in the margins) and specify the level of protection for each portion. Original documents made available for inspection need not be designated until after the inspecting Party identifies what it wants copied; during inspection, all material is deemed “HIGHLY CONFIDENTIAL – ATTORNEYS’ EYES ONLY.”

rubrics_metrics.name: Manner and timing of designations for testimony and transcripts
rubrics_metrics.description: For testimony given in depositions or other pretrial or trial proceedings, the Designating Party must identify on the record, before the close of the deposition/hearing/proceeding, all protected testimony and specify the level of protection being asserted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If impractical to identify portions on the record, the Designating Party may invoke a right to have up to 21 days to identify specific portions; only those portions designated within 21 days are covered. Alternatively the Designating Party may specify the entire transcript be treated as “CONFIDENTIAL” or “HIGHLY CONFIDENTIAL – ATTORNEYS’ EYES ONLY” at deposition or within 21 days. Transcripts prepared before expiration of the 21-day period are treated as if designated AEO in their entirety during that period. Transcripts must have an obvious legend on the title page and a following list of pages/line numbers designated and their protection level; the Designating Party must inform the court reporter of these requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manner and timing of designations for other tangible items
rubrics_metrics.description: For information produced in some form other than documentary and for any other tangible items, the Producing Party must affix in a prominent place on the exterior of the container the appropriate legend.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If only portions of the information/item warrant protection, the Producing Party shall, to the extent practicable, identify the protected portions and specify the level of protection being asserted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inadvertent failures to designate
rubrics_metrics.description: If timely corrected, an inadvertent failure to designate qualified information or items does not, standing alone, waive the Designating Party’s right to secure protection under this Order for such material.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Upon timely correction of a designation, the Receiving Party must make reasonable efforts to ensure the material is treated in accordance with the Order’s provisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing for challenging confidentiality designations
rubrics_metrics.description: Any Party or Non-Party may challenge a designation of confidentiality at any time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Unless prompt challenge is necessary to avoid foreseeable substantial unfairness, unnecessary economic burdens, or significant disruption/delay, a Party does not waive the right to challenge by electing not to mount a prompt challenge after the original designation is disclosed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Meet-and-confer requirement for challenges
rubrics_metrics.description: The Challenging Party shall initiate the dispute resolution process by providing written notice of each designation it is challenging and describing the basis for each challenge, and must begin conferring directly (voice-to-voice) within 14 days of service of notice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Written notice must state the challenge is made pursuant to this paragraph. In conferring, the Challenging Party must explain why the designation is improper and give the Designating Party an opportunity to review, reconsider, or explain the designation. A Challenging Party may proceed to judicial steps only after the meet-and-confer or upon showing the Designating Party unwilling to participate timely.

rubrics_metrics.name: Judicial intervention procedure for designation disputes
rubrics_metrics.description: If parties cannot resolve a challenge, the Designating Party must file a motion to retain confidentiality under Civil Local Rule 7 (and Civil Local Rule 79-5 if applicable) within 21 days of the initial notice of challenge or within 14 days of agreement that the meet-and-confer will not resolve the dispute, whichever is earlier.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each motion must be accompanied by a competent declaration affirming compliance with meet-and-confer requirements. Failure to file such a motion with the required declaration within the deadline automatically waives the confidentiality designation for each challenged designation. The burden of persuasion is on the Designating Party. Frivolous or improper-purpose challenges may expose the Challenging Party to sanctions. Material remains under its designated protection until the court rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Basic principles governing access and use of Protected Material
rubrics_metrics.description: A Receiving Party may use Protected Material disclosed or produced by another Party or Non-Party in connection with this case only for prosecuting, defending, or attempting to settle this litigation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Protected Material may be disclosed only to categories of persons and under conditions described in the Order. When litigation terminates, Receiving Party must comply with final disposition provisions. Protected Material must be stored and maintained at a location and in a secure manner that ensures access is limited to authorized persons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authorized disclosure recipients for 'CONFIDENTIAL' material
rubrics_metrics.description: Unless otherwise ordered or permitted, a Receiving Party may disclose 'CONFIDENTIAL' information only to specified categories of persons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permitted recipients include: (a) Receiving Party’s Outside Counsel of Record and necessary employees who have signed Exhibit A; (b) officers, directors, employees (including House Counsel) to whom disclosure is reasonably necessary and who signed Exhibit A; (c) Experts who signed Exhibit A and for whom disclosure is reasonably necessary; (d) the court and its personnel; (e) court reporters, professional jury/trial consultants, Professional Vendors who signed Exhibit A; (f) witnesses during depositions who signed Exhibit A (with deposition pages revealing Protected Material separately bound and limited in disclosure); and (g) the author or recipient of the document or custodian or other person who possessed or knew the information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authorized disclosure recipients for 'HIGHLY CONFIDENTIAL – ATTORNEYS’ EYES ONLY' and 'HIGHLY CONFIDENTIAL – SOURCE CODE' material
rubrics_metrics.description: Unless otherwise ordered or permitted, a Receiving Party may disclose AEO or SOURCE CODE designated information only to a narrower list of recipients.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permitted recipients include: (a) Receiving Party’s Outside Counsel of Record and necessary employees who signed Exhibit A; (b) Designated House Counsel subject to qualification procedures in paragraph 7.4(a)(1); (c) Experts subject to qualification procedures in paragraph 7.4(a)(2); (d) the court and its personnel; (e) court reporters, consultants, and Professional Vendors who signed Exhibit A; and (f) the author or recipient or custodian who possessed or knew the information. Note: Designated House Counsel shall not have access to 'HIGHLY CONFIDENTIAL – SOURCE CODE.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedures for approving disclosure to Designated House Counsel
rubrics_metrics.description: A Party seeking to disclose AEO material to Designated House Counsel must make a written request to the Designating Party containing specific identifying and job-duty information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Request must set forth full name, city/state of residence, and describe current and reasonably foreseeable primary job duties/responsibilities in sufficient detail to determine involvement in competitive decision-making. Designating Party has 14 days to object in writing with detailed grounds; if objected, parties must meet-and-confer within seven days of objection; if unresolved, the seeker may file a motion under Civil Local Rule 7 with specified content including risk assessment and additional safeguards. The opposing party bears burden of proving risk of harm outweighs the need for disclosure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedures for approving disclosure to Experts
rubrics_metrics.description: A Party seeking to disclose AEO or SOURCE CODE material to an Expert must make a written request including detailed information about the Expert and the categories of information to be disclosed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Request must identify categories of information to disclose, Expert’s full name and city/state of residence, attach current resume, identify current employer(s), list persons/entities who paid or received compensation from the Expert in relevant areas during preceding five years, and identify litigation where Expert offered testimony in preceding five years (name, number, filing date, court). If Expert claims third-party confidentiality obligations, provide whatever can be disclosed and be available to meet-and-confer. Designating Party has 14 days to object; meet-and-confer and motion procedures mirror those for Designated House Counsel. The opposing party bears burden to prove harm outweighs need.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prosecution bar
rubrics_metrics.description: Absent written consent from the Producing Party, any individual who receives access to AEO or SOURCE CODE information shall not be involved in prosecution of patents or patent applications relating to the subject matter of this action before any foreign or domestic agency, including the Patent Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prosecution includes drafting, amending, advising, or otherwise affecting scope or maintenance of patent claims (but does not include representing a party challenging a patent before an agency). The Prosecution Bar begins when access is first received and ends two (2) years after final termination of the action. Examples: original prosecution, reissue, and reexamination proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Designation and special protections for Source Code
rubrics_metrics.description: A Producing Party may designate source code as 'HIGHLY CONFIDENTIAL – SOURCE CODE' if it comprises confidential, proprietary, or trade secret source code. SOURCE CODE receives all protections afforded AEO information, including the Prosecution Bar, except Designated House Counsel are excluded from access.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Source code inspection: made available for inspection in a format allowing reasonable review/search, during normal business hours at Producing Party counsel’s office or another agreed location, on a secured computer in a secured room without Internet or network access. Receiving Party shall not copy, remove, or otherwise transfer any portion onto recordable media. Producing Party may visually monitor reviewers to ensure no unauthorized recording/copying/transmission. Receiving Party may request paper copies of limited portions reasonably necessary for court filings, depositions, trial, or expert reports; Producing Party must provide requested portions in paper form with bates and 'HIGHLY CONFIDENTIAL – SOURCE CODE' label, and may challenge the amount requested under dispute resolution and timeframes of Paragraph 6. Receiving Party must maintain a record of any individual who inspected source code and keep paper copies in a secured locked area, must not create electronic images of paper copies or convert their information into electronic format, and may only make additional paper copies when necessary for filings, depositions, or preparation of the case. Any paper copies used during deposition must be retrieved by the Producing Party at the end of each day and not left with court reporters or unauthorized individuals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protected material subpoenaed or ordered produced in other litigation
rubrics_metrics.description: If a Party is served with a subpoena or court order in other litigation compelling disclosure of information designated in this action as CONFIDENTIAL/AEO/SOURCE CODE, that Party must promptly notify the Designating Party in writing and provide a copy of the subpoena or order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also promptly notify in writing the party who caused the subpoena/ order in the other litigation that some or all of the material is subject to this Protective Order and include a copy of the Order; cooperate with reasonable procedures sought by the Designating Party. If Designating Party timely seeks a protective order, the served Party shall not produce the designated information before determination by that court without permission. The Designating Party bears the burden and expense of seeking protection in that court. Nothing authorizes disobeying a lawful directive of another court.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-Party’s protected material produced in this litigation
rubrics_metrics.description: The terms of this Order apply to information produced by a Non-Party and designated as CONFIDENTIAL/AEO/SOURCE CODE; such information is protected by the remedies and relief in this Order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a Party is required by a valid discovery request to produce a Non-Party’s confidential information and is subject to an agreement not to produce it, then the Party must promptly notify in writing the Requesting Party and the Non-Party, provide the Non-Party a copy of the Protective Order, the discovery request(s), and a reasonably specific description of the information requested, and make the information available for inspection by the Non-Party. If the Non-Party fails to object or seek protection within 14 days, the Receiving Party may produce responsive information. If Non-Party seeks protection timely, the Receiving Party shall not produce the information before the court’s determination. Absent court order to the contrary, the Non-Party bears the burden and expense of seeking protection in this court.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unauthorized disclosure of Protected Material
rubrics_metrics.description: If a Receiving Party learns it has disclosed Protected Material to any person or in any circumstance not authorized under this Order, it must take immediate remedial steps.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Obligations: (a) notify in writing the Designating Party of the unauthorized disclosures; (b) use best efforts to retrieve all unauthorized copies; (c) inform the person(s) who received unauthorized disclosures of all terms of the Order; and (d) request such person(s) execute the 'Acknowledgment and Agreement to Be Bound' (Exhibit A).

rubrics_metrics.name: Inadvertent production of privileged or otherwise protected material
rubrics_metrics.description: When a Producing Party notifies Receiving Parties that certain inadvertently produced material is subject to a claim of privilege or other protection, the obligations of Receiving Parties are those set forth in Federal Rule of Civil Procedure 26(b)(5)(B).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This provision is not intended to modify e-discovery procedures that provide for production without prior privilege review. Pursuant to Federal Rule of Evidence 502(d) and (e), parties may incorporate their agreement on the effect of disclosure of privileged or work-product material in a stipulated protective order submitted to the court.

rubrics_metrics.name: Right to further relief and to assert other objections
rubrics_metrics.description: Nothing in this Order abridges the right of any person to seek modification by the court in the future, nor waives any Party’s right to object to disclosure or production on any ground not addressed in this Protective Order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Similarly, no Party waives any right to object on any ground to use in evidence any of the material covered by this Protective Order.

rubrics_metrics.name: Export control compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: Disclosure of Protected Material shall be subject to all applicable laws and regulations relating to the export of technical data contained in such Protected Material, including release to foreign persons or nationals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Producing Party is responsible for identifying controlled technical data; the Receiving Party must take measures necessary to ensure compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing Protected Material under seal
rubrics_metrics.description: Without written permission from the Designating Party or a court order after appropriate notice, a Party may not file any Protected Material in the public record in this action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A Party seeking to file under seal must comply with Civil Local Rule 79-5; Protected Material may be filed under seal only pursuant to a court order authorizing sealing of the specific Protected Material at issue, and a sealing order will issue only upon a request establishing that the Protected Material is privileged, protectable as a trade secret, or otherwise entitled to protection under the law. If a request to file under seal pursuant to Civil Local Rule 79-5(e) is denied, the Receiving Party may file the Protected Material in the public record pursuant to Civil Local Rule 79-5(e)(2) unless otherwise instructed by the court.

rubrics_metrics.name: Final disposition of Protected Material
rubrics_metrics.description: Within 60 days after final disposition of this action, each Receiving Party must return all Protected Material to the Producing Party or destroy such material.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 'All Protected Material' includes all copies, abstracts, compilations, summaries, and any other format reproducing or capturing any of the Protected Material. Whether returned or destroyed, the Receiving Party must submit a written certification by the 60-day deadline identifying all Protected Material returned or destroyed and affirming no retained copies remain. Counsel are entitled to retain an archival copy of pleadings, motion papers, transcripts, legal memoranda, correspondence, exhibits, expert reports, attorney work product, and consultant/expert work product even if such materials contain Protected Material; any such archival copies containing Protected Material remain subject to this Protective Order as set forth in Section 4 (DURATION).
